1.explanation:
• StyledMeter.js: this file injects the CSS transition on all path properties (transition: all 300ms), causing Chrome to animate the path’s geometry (the d attribute) rather than just the stroke offset. 
• Circle.js: this component builds and renders the actual <path> for a circle meter, setting new d, strokeDasharray, and strokeDashoffset whenever the value changes. Because transition: all is in effect, changes to d are animated (morphing) instead of just the stroke offset.  
• Meter.js: this is the top‐level logic that chooses between bar and circle types, passes the transition timing into StyledMeter, and triggers the re‐render. It must be updated or given finer‐grained props so that only the stroke‐dashoffset is animated, not the entire path shape.
1.bug_scenario: When you render a Meter of type “circle” in Chrome and update its value, the SVG <path> that draws the arc is styled with a blanket “transition: all 300ms” rule. Chrome will animate every attribute change on the path (including its d attribute) over 300 ms, producing a visibly warped, “morphing” effect. In Firefox and Safari the d attribute isn’t transitioned so the arc simply jumps to its new geometry and you don’t see the glitch. What you want instead is a smooth radial animation of the stroke around the circle, not a shape‐morph transition of the path data.

2.explanation:
• StyledMeter.js: This file applies “transition: all 300ms …” to every <path> in the Meter’s SVG, causing Chrome to interpolate the entire path definition (the 'd' attribute) rather than just the stroke length. Removing or narrowing that transition here is the primary fix.  
• Circle.js: This is where the circular arc <path> is created and its stroke-dasharray is set. It inherits the transition from StyledMeter.js, so it’s directly affected by the over-broad CSS rule. You may need to override style here or adjust which properties get transitioned.  
• utils.js: Contains the functions that compute the SVG arc path string and dash array values used by Circle.js. While not strictly a CSS file, it underpins the path data being animated. If you switch to animating only stroke-dasharray, you should confirm these calculations still produce correct values.  
• Meter.js: Chooses between Bar and Circle types and props. Changing how transition timing or style props flow into the Circle type will likely involve updates here—e.g. passing a more specific transition prop or disabling transition by default for circle type.
2.bug_scenario: When you click to change the value on a circular Meter in Chrome, the SVG path is redrawn with a “transition: all 300ms” on the <path> element, so Chrome interpolates the entire path shape and you see a wild, distorted morphing as it moves from one arc to the next. In Firefox and Safari the <path> ’d’ attribute changes aren’t animated, so you see no animation at all. The desired behavior is a smooth, radial arc transition (ideally animating only the stroke-dasharray), not a shape-morphing animation.
